segments.text: Gummy stands outside in the cold, shivering.
It's easy to think shivering just means you're worn out.
But actually, shivering is something your body does on purpose.
Skin sensors send a signal to the brain.
The brain tells the muscles to move fast.
The muscles rapidly tighten and relax.
That very motion creates heat in the body.
Now that shivering is warming the body up.
The brain moves the muscles to warm the body itself.
